title: Glasgow could see 20 meteors an hour as debris from Halley's comet returns
excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower may be seen over Glasgow later this week as the Earth passes through a stream of tiny debris left behind by Halley's comet.
content:
A meteor shower may be seen over Glasgow later this week as the Earth passes through a stream of tiny debris left behind by Halley's comet.

The annual Orionid meteor shower occurs every October, with this year's shower expected to reach its peak during the night of October 21-22, according to NASA.

However, it could be visible for several days on either side of this date.

People in Glasgow won't see Halley's comet itself, but may see between 10 and 20 Orionid meteors per hour if the conditions are right.

Moonlight could interfere with the ability to see the meteors as it will be in its waxing gibbous phase, and the Met Office forecast for Glasgow for the night of October 21-22 currently shows it will be cloudy overnight.

Royal Museums Greenwich says for the best conditions, you need to find a safe location away from street lights and other sources of light pollution, and they can be seen with the naked eye.

The Orionid meteor shower is caused by cometary debris entering the Earth's atmosphere at speeds of around 41 miles per second and vaporising from friction with the air, causing streaks of light.

Halley's comet comes by Earth once every 75-76 years.
